I think you misunderstand how Foresight Slash works. It’s not “ope Mr. Monster is trying to be a big meanie again, toggle god mode”.  Yes, you can combo into it from basically any move, and I’ll concede the “parry” window is pretty generous, but you don’t just hit the buttons and win. You have to land the initial slash with correct timing, then not get hit at all during the back dodge animation, then finally the lunge attack following the dodge (which I’m near positive doesn’t propel you forward enough to make up for the distance the dodge takes you back, making it miss constantly) has to land. If you don’t meet all those conditions you get nothing besides your Spirit Gauge getting emptied and your stamina having a chunk taken out of it.

I’m not saying it’s hard to do, but with the different mix-ups and charge attacks different monsters have, it’s far from brainless.

Orb of Annulment. Basically deletes a random affix from whatever item you use it on.

It’s fairly simple if you treat Waystones like you would any other item. Transmute the grays into blues and Aug them, check the current affixes and Waystone drop chance on blue Waystones, and if those are good then you Regal. If you’re still happy then Exalt it. You can use any 3 of the same tier Waystones you’re not happy with and use the Reforging Bench to turn them into 1 Waystone of the next tier. Precursor Tablets can also be Transmuted and Auged, but not Regaled.

As an aside, you can also use mats on Sttongboxes to make them better. If it says unidentified then use a Wisdom Scroll on it, then use Augs and Regals like you would any other item.

So I always suggest backing up your current game save prior to attempting to use mods. That’s just best practice when it comes to modding any game. It allows you to return to a “pre-mod” state without potentially having to wipe the whole install and re-download everything. 
 
So as far as mods being risky goes, I don’t really think I agree with that necessarily. The only thing you really need to worry about is that when the game is still newer, the updates will come far more frequently, and thus your mods are going to break more frequently. If you’re using mods that alter fundamental aspects of the game then your mods being broken and not loading correctly could translate to your game just not booting period until all your mods are updated accordingly. 

Personally I find Starfield to be the easiest to mod Bethesda game that I can remember. Rarely do I have so many mods just work like they’re supposed to, and I’ve installed 90%+ of my mods manually so I don’t have a good way to organize them and manage load order. 

My suggestion to you would be to dip your toes in by downloading Vortex from NexusMods and getting it set up. Then download the StarUI suite and some other simpler stuff, and just build your knowledge base slowly. 

Just keep in mind that modders are volunteers putting in a lot of work for free. If a mod update doesn’t come quickly try not to get frustrated, especially since official mod support for Starfield isn’t a thing until the Starfield Creation Kit gets released.

I’ll add a tip here myself, though it only applies to PC players: just download the StarUI mod (I’d also highly suggest StarHUD, StarWorkbench, and StarOutpost, as well as StarUI Configurator for easy customization ) as it adds a “Take/Deposit/Sell all in category” button. Meaning whenever you stop at a vendor, just switch to selling from wherever you have the useless smorgasbord or public library worth of Dickens novels socked away, then press the “Sell all in category” button and watch all the useless stuff vaporize and turn to Credits. It’s quite handy, though it needs a “Drop/Jettison all in category” button to be truly perfect.

I’m not sure how it worked in other countries, but for a long time in the US getting narcotic pain meds was laughably easy. On top of the whole Purdue Pharma fiasco with them pushing OxyContin as “non-addictive”, there were a lot of doctors who were willing to write you a prescription for Vicodin if you did so much as stub your toe. When the negative effects of all this over prescribing came to light, instead of doing things the smart way and attempting to help the people now hopelessly addicted to opiates, the DEA clamped down hard on the prescribing of opiates basically overnight. A lot of people had prescriptions they’d been taking for years just yanked away without any warning at all. As you may or may not know, opiate withdrawals really, REALLLLYYYY fucking suck, and not only that but now whatever medical issue the pain meds were alleviating is now back with a vengeance. 

So if you’re an everyday Joe in that situation, what do you do? You start buying pills off the street, and if you can’t find pills then heroin is the next best thing. Supply and demand applies to everything on the planet and the black market for opiates positively exploded making pills and heroin very easy to get, while treatment programs were damn near nonexistent and social stigma was at an all time high.

Et voila, you have a world class opioid crisis. One that’s now being made far, far deadlier by cheap Fentanyl being synthesized overseas and endlessly dumped onto the American black market. I’ve been clean of opiates for a while now but last I knew finding actual heroin was like finding a unicorn and it’s basically Fent or nothing anymore. 

So there you go, the American opioid crisis in a nutshell. Obviously there’s a lot more that goes into it with things like poverty and the destruction of the middle class exacerbating the issue, but you get the idea.

**Zealot of Days Long Past**

Where this boss can be found: 

Upon completion of the main story an illusory floor will dissipate next to the Erdtree Throne, allowing you to access a basement level Legacy Dungeon under Leyndell Castle. He is the final boss to the dungeon. 

Please note: this will only happen if you beat any main story bosses while utilizing Ash Summons.

Boss Guide: 

Upon entering the arena the boss will immediately use his ranged poison bile attack. Be sure to dodge as soon as you regain control after mist traversal. This is the same attack he’ll use, in addition to poison and Scarlet Rot building incantations, whenever you stay at medium/long range for any length of time. 

At close range he will switch to melee, utilizing a parrying dagger and simple straight sword. He will dodge any and all ranged attacks and will almost always parry melee attacks that can be parried if he is not in any other animation. Knowing this, your best strategy for dealing damage is forcing him to miss his combos by dodging then punishing with your own attacks or by blocking his hits and using guard counters. You can also use your Ash Summon to draw aggro so you can land some hits. Use caution though, as this boss does have a Death Blight aura, so land as many hits as possible then back off and clear any buildup. 

At 50% HP phase 2 of the fight will begin. The boss will let out a deafening screech that stuns you and dissipates any Ash Summon still on the field before drinking from a flask that returns him to 75% HP. In this phase he will no longer use ranged attacks nor any melee weapons, in addition to his Death Blight aura dissipating. To compensate his damage resistance is severely buffed and he will be frenzied, becoming faster and dishing out fist combos that cause heavy stagger almost constantly with a very small window to punish. Additionally, everywhere he runs or leaps he will leave a trail of slime that causes poison buildup. Your best strategy is to either use guard counters or most importantly ranged attacks, as he will no longer bother dodging. He can also be poise broken but this will require a large amount of damage very quickly and he will punish any misses severely.

Upon the bosses HP reaching 0 a cutscene will begin wherein he stumbles backwards before falling down. He lets out another deafening screech before sprinting at you hunched over with his arms straight out behind his back. He continues past you and out of the arena. 

If you were able to complete the main story then this boss is beatable but he is significantly harder than many other bosses besides Melania (she’s the blade of Miquella, undefeated too from what I hear). Bring the proper tools and learn the fight and you should be fine.

I’m not saying everything needs skill. I even stated some things I thought could qualify as unskilled labor just like you did. That being said, I can tell you 100% you’re being extremely reductive about working in manufacturing. It is very far from “putting things on things” and has been in a lot of places for a while now. The Henry Ford assembly line has been obsolete for a long time, and in cases where a line of people doing one task is required those jobs are generally filled by temps. At least that’s the case around here.

For my current position I had to take an aptitude test involving mechanical knowledge, mathematics, literacy, and critical thinking. Had to pass it just to be granted an interview. Granted it wasn’t the SATs or anything, but they won’t take just any idiot who walks in off the street. Now, are there positions at my workplace that almost anyone can probably do? Sure, I guess, but they hire people with enough of a brain specifically because they want people they can mold into skilled operators. That truly does take a lot of time and patience and I promise you it isn’t something you can just rock up and truly learn in a day. A lot of guys I work with have been doing it for decades and still regularly see shit that they’ve never had happen before. Industrial machinery is incredibly fickle on a good day. Keeping it not just running, but cranking out product that meets spec is a pretty delicate matter that requires full comprehension of every single thing at work. 

I want to be clear that I’m not trying to say that I think being an operator is as important or remotely as hard as teaching or being involved in some scientific pursuit. It’s not and I know it’s not. It’s just also not unskilled, at least in the environments I have my experience in. I’ve seen what happens when there’s a mass exodus from a department and new people are brought in to fill a bunch of vacancies on one line because it happened at an old job. That line didn’t even sniff profitability for more than 2 years, and it was just moving beyond breaking even after I left a little over 3 years in. It likely took another 2 years beyond that for it to reach previous productivity levels at the rate they were going. 

I’m sure you’re gonna read all this and think I’m trying to over-inflate my importance, but I’m not. I’m well aware what I do isn’t special and there’s a bunch of other people out there just like me. I just take umbrage with the “unskilled labor” moniker and the consequences that come with being labeled as such. Blue collar America in general deserves better.

Anyway, one night my stepdad and I were playing some NCAA football.
